name: Retrovael
description: Retrovael is a hippocampal reactivation agent that, when combined with BCI memory-indexing protocols, allows users to re-experience stored autobiographical memories at near-full fidelity — not as recollection but as genuine re-living, with all sensory and emotional content restored. Originally developed for trauma processing therapy, it was rapidly adopted recreationally when users discovered that positive memories could be replayed indefinitely. The drug is Lazarus's most ethically contested product.
effects: vivid first-person re-experiencing of selected memories
full emotional and sensory restoration of the memory
sense of temporal presence in the past moment
profound comfort and joy from positive memories
BCI users can share memory-streams with consenting partners
side_effects: reality appears dull and thin after use
progressive difficulty forming new positive memories as old ones are preferred
memory degradation — replayed memories become corrupted over time, losing fidelity
severe depression when access is lost
rare: users enter self-sustaining memory loops and cannot exit without medical intervention
cultural_context: Retrovael is GLMZ's most quietly devastating addiction. It is prescribed legally for grief counseling and PTSD, but recreational use is rampant among Tier 3-4 users who are old enough to have memories worth revisiting and wealthy enough to afford it. There are support communities — called 'Archive Anonymous' — for users trying to return to present life. The cruelest irony is that the memories degrade with each replay, becoming less accurate until users are reliving distorted echoes of experiences they've destroyed.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive hasn't left his apartment in three months — he's been replaying the same six months of his life, when his daughter was young, but the memories are now so corrupted he's forgotten what she actually looked like
A black-market dealer is selling Retrovael pre-loaded with fabricated 'ideal memories' — beautiful experiences the user never had — and the demand is overwhelming
A grief counselor with a legitimate Retrovael prescription discovers her patient is replaying not his own memories but illegally archived memories of his deceased wife, purchased from a data broker
